```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(coherentSurv)
```

The same event-history interface can represent subjects in different fields.
Its applicability still depends on the observation model, independent-unit
definition, sufficient retained history and absorbing endpoint. Renaming a
patient as a machine does not verify those assumptions in a new application.

## Cross-discipline translation table

| Contract or target | Clinical trial | Health-system study | Fleet reliability | Credit study |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| Independent unit (`unit`) | Participant | Patient | Device | Account or borrower; declare which |
| Time (`time_unit`) | Time since randomization | Time since an eligible index date | Operating hours | Time since origination or another justified process origin |
| Recurrent marks (`event_types`) | Recurrent admissions or toxicity episodes | Defined acute-care episodes | Faults or repairs | Defined delinquency or covenant episodes |
| Absorbing endpoint (`terminal`) | Death or another explicitly terminal study endpoint | Death | Irreversible failure | Default defined as irreversible within this analysis |
| Observation windows | Known episodes detected between scans | Rounded dates with known recorded counts | Batched fault logs | Recorded episodes reported in intervals |
| Predictable history | Prior defined episodes | Previously observed care | Previous observed faults | Previous recorded distress episodes |
| Working frailty | Residual subject heterogeneity | Residual patient heterogeneity | Residual device heterogeneity | Residual account heterogeneity |
| `risk` | Terminal-event probability by the horizon | Death risk by the horizon | Failure probability | Default probability |
| `burden_<mark>` | Expected episodes before absorption | Expected defined encounters before death | Expected fault/repair counts before failure | Expected distress episodes before default |
| `survival` | Probability alive/nonterminal at the horizon | Survival probability | Probability operational/nonterminal | Probability not in the terminal default state |
| `time_alive` | Restricted mean time alive | Restricted mean time alive | Restricted expected time before failure | Restricted expected time before default |
| Finite-support sensitivity | Declared incomplete recording experiment | Declared out-of-network recording experiment | Declared incomplete logging experiment | Declared incomplete distress reporting experiment |

The package's `unit` argument names the identifier column; its default column is
`id`. The `event_type` argument names the mark column. No-event rows use `"0"`,
`"none"` or an empty string, not missing values. `terminal` is binary 0/1. Terminal
causes in a competing-risk wrapper are distinct from recurrent marks.

The `time_alive` target integrates survival over a finite future horizon. It is
not automatically time without morbidity, community-dwelling days, quality-
adjusted survival, unrestricted mean failure time or discounted performing
value. Those require explicitly defined states, rewards or valuation models.
Frailty is a working heterogeneity model; it does not identify a biological
mechanism, stress process or borrower preference.

## A reproducible relabelling check

```{r relabel}
raw <- cs_simulate(30, horizon = 1, rates = c(.8, .4, .3), seed = 1126,
                   censor_rate = 0, time_unit = "years")
clinical <- raw
clinical$event_type <- c("0", "admission", "toxicity")[raw$event_type + 1L]
engineering <- raw
engineering$event_type <- c("0", "repair", "fault")[raw$event_type + 1L]
a <- cs_as_trajectory(clinical, event_types = c("admission", "toxicity"),
                       time_unit = "years")
b <- cs_as_trajectory(engineering, event_types = c("repair", "fault"),
                       time_unit = "years")
stopifnot(identical(a$.cs_mark, b$.cs_mark),
          identical(a$.cs_terminal, b$.cs_terminal),
          identical(unname(cs_build_history(a)$counts), unname(cs_build_history(b)$counts)))
data.frame(records = nrow(a), units = length(unique(a$id)),
           terminal_events = sum(a$terminal))
```

This verifies only label-invariance of the declared data contract. It is one
synthetic dataset represented twice, not evidence from two populations.

## Choosing a model and a report

Use `cs_fit()` for the supported shared-law likelihood and `predict()` for
prognostic forecasts. Use `cs_surv()` or `cs_competing()` for their documented
standard regimes. Treatment effects use the separate `cs_causal()` interface
under its baseline-treatment assumptions; a prognostic covariate coefficient
is not automatically a causal effect.

Use `cs_bounds()` or `cs_bounds_sparse()` only with an explicit finite-support
recorded law, target payoff and recording restrictions. A timing fibre with
known counts does not reconstruct episodes that were never recorded. Losses
from unobserved events, uncertainty about model parameters and numerical
truncation remain different quantities.

For economics or policy, supply an explicit cost or reward model. Counts do not
by themselves estimate expenditure, financial expected loss or policy welfare.
Dependence among accounts of one borrower, devices in one fleet or members of
one household also requires an appropriate independent-unit/model definition.
Administrative follow-up loss is not an absorbing clinical or economic event.

## Runnable companion tutorials

- *Predictive maintenance and fleet reliability*: synthetic faults, eligibility
  and common-law forecasting, with a separately declared observation example.
- *Clinical-trial estimands*: synthetic baseline randomization and the causal
  interface, with explicit estimand and censoring definitions.
- *Credit risk and default*: synthetic distress events and restricted performing
  life, with separately specified monetary assumptions and sensitivity support.
- *Source mapping and environment diagnostics*: scoped ADTTE/OMOP mappings,
  audit provenance and offline numerical checks.

These tutorials are software demonstrations, not external clinical, engineering
or financial validation. Use the same installed R package from Python through
the supplied rpy2 or Rscript example; study definitions and observation assumptions
remain the analyst's responsibility in either language.
